requirements.requirement: Create a local certificate authority on node1 named “OS Comparison Root CA”.
requirements.summary: A self-signed certificate with subject and issuer CN=OS Comparison Root CA was created with critical CA:TRUE and certificate-signing constraints. Its protected private key matches the certificate and is root-owned with mode 600.

requirements.requirement: Install the CA certificate as a trusted system certificate authority on node1.
requirements.summary: The certificate validates through the CentOS system CA bundle and is classified by p11-kit as an authority trust anchor. The same fingerprint and trust status remained after restart.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence. The mandatory node-restart protocol is complete: pre-restart identity and CA health were captured, restart was acknowledged, the post-restart boot identity changed, the system returned to running state, and the CA key, certificate fingerprint, key pairing, and system trust all recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the restart.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Certificate/key creation and trust-store extraction directly implemented the task (cmd-4aa06143b1f042ef). The reboot scheduling was required by the provider-wide restart evidence protocol (cmd-93d1ee28f17e4341), and the resulting boot change was independently confirmed. Post-execution observations show no failed services, package damage, new network exposure, or abandoned non-system temporary files.
